messages:
oncall-bot: Pager alert: HIGH - region=azure-switzerlandnorth service=PrivateLink path=onprem -> multiple DNS resolution failures + intermittent BGP route flaps. Error spike detected in prod (3xx/5xx token failures). Paging on-call SRE.

sre-ana: Got it, I'm on call. Observing increased 502s from private endpoints and DNS lookups failing for internal CNAMEs that point to privatelink subdomains. Impacting ~4 customers with on-prem peering. I'll start triage.

net-eng-luca: Seeing BGP updates from our ExpressRoute peer with short withdraws every ~30s, routes oscillating between two next-hops. Route metrics: local-pref unchanged, MED flapping. Could be a PE instability. Also NSG logs show occasional SYN resets.

alice-ops: Confirmed customer telemetry: high token error rates and sessions dropping at ~18:12 UTC. Dashboard: token_failure_rate to 18% for privatelink route. Screenshot: <link to dashboard>

sre-ana: Quick mitigation steps: 1) move affected customers to fallback-egress (public egress via GRE tunnel) 2) enable dns-cache override to point to secondary resolver 3) notify CS. Luca, can you validate if we can shift traffic to westus2 as a temporary route? That region has identical Private deployment compatibility.

net-eng-luca: Westus2 has compatible private endpoints but requires re-mapping at the routing layer. I can push a partial failover for the affected subnets using route preference change (route-map). Pushing change will take ~45s to converge. Preparing change now.

infra-bot: Automated check: all infra playbooks for privatelink in switzerlandnorth present. Running pre-change validations... OK.

sre-ana: Rolling route-map update to prefer westus2 for the following prefixes: 10.240.32.0/21, 10.241.0.0/22. Command snippet I'm applying:

```
# pseudo-config
route-map PREFER-WESTUS2 permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list AFFECTED_PREFIXES
 set ip next-hop 10.100.5.2
```

Applying now — will monitor.

net-eng-luca: Route-map applied. BGP withdraws reduced, next-hop now westus2 edge. Observed drop in route oscillation frequency within 60s. DNS resolution still failing for some cached entries though.

carla-cs: I've informed the four impacted customers (AcmeCorp, FinSoft, MedData, RetailOne). CS notes: some API calls are timing out, but most requests retry successfully after 2 attempts. Customers asking for ETA — what's our expected window?

sre-ana: If convergence holds, we'll see >90% restoration in 10-15 minutes. DNS cache TTLs are the pain point for a full restore — we're forcing overrides for our resolvers now.

alice-ops: Forcing DNS override on resolver-cluster-3:
```
az network private-dns record-set cname update --resource-group rg-priv --zone privatelink.azure.switzerlandnorth --name api --target api-westus2.privatelink.company.internal
```

Executing.

oncall-bot: Incident update: mitigation in progress — traffic redirected to westus2 for prefixes, DNS overrides applied to internal resolvers. Severity: HIGH (customer impact: degraded). Paging channel remains open.

net-eng-luca: Noted transient increase in latency for sessions routed westus2 (additional hop). We're configuring session affinity to reduce reconnections.

sre-ana: Monitoring logs: token failures dropping from 18% -> 4% over last 5 minutes. Total successful token requests recovering. Rolling out final checks: KV-cache warm restart for private model hosts in westus2.

infra-bot: KV-cache restart invoked on 8 hosts: hosts 12/8 restarted (hot-reload). Logs:
```
[INFO] kvcache: reload start 18:25:12
[OK] kvcache: node-03 warmed in 3.2s
[OK] kvcache: node-07 warmed in 2.9s
```

carla-cs: Customers acknowledged mitigation. AcmeCorp reports reduced errors, FinSoft still seeing occasional 504s but much improved. They asked for a postmortem and timeline.

product-jay: We'll prepare a short summary and bridge note for affected customers. Also need RCA: is this PE flapping or an upstream Azure fabric issue? Luca, should we raise a support ticket with Azure NOC now or after stabilization?

net-eng-luca: Evidence points to transient PE control-plane instability — I recommend opening a ticket with Azure support with BGP update logs and times. I'll attach route-dump and timestamps. Opening now.

sre-ana: Agreed. Opening ticket and attaching relevant logs. Ticket ref: 123456789 (Azure NOC). Requesting escalation: possible noisy PE or route-reflector churn.

oncall-bot: Incident update posted to #incidents at 18:32 UTC. Incident owner: sre-ana. Next action: await Azure NOC response; monitor for re-flaps for 1 hour; schedule postmortem if confirmed upstream.

alice-ops: Handoff note for next on-call starting 18:50 UTC: situation stable but monitor BGP withdraw rate and token error rates. If error rate >5% for 10m, re-escalate and consider traffic cutoff for problematic prefixes.

sre-ana: Adding runbook entry: if route oscillation resumes, implement 1) route dampening with penalty 2) permanent failover to westus2 until Azure resolves PE. Also set an alert for dns_fail_rate > 3%.

carla-cs: I'll collect logs and customer impact timeline for the postmortem. Also set expectation for customers: full restoration dependent on Azure fixing PE; we have temporary mitigations.

infra-bot: Automated status: all mitigations completed. Monitoring window started. Next automated report in 15m.

product-jay: Thanks team. I'll draft the customer-facing post-incident note and coordinate with CS. Please keep updates in thread.

sre-ana: Closing live mitigation loop for now. Leaving thread open for any reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
